title: Fix audio quality (choppy + wind/airy)
summary: Fixed the poor audio quality reported by the user. Root cause was a broken 48 kHz→16 kHz decimation in audio.js: a one-pole low-pass with alpha=0.15 produced a ~1.1 kHz cutoff (muffled speech) and naive decimate-by-3 aliased into the 'wind/air' noise. Replaced with sending clean 48 kHz PCM verbatim (RNNoise kept at native rate), switched the playback AudioContext to 48 kHz, added a priming/jitter buffer in the player worklet to absorb WebSocket bursts (fixing choppiness), relaxed the 'No audio' warning to sustained starvation only, and batched ~20 ms of frames per WebSocket message to cut overhead.
userVisibleChange: Audio is now clear and intelligible (no muffling/aliasing) and no longer choppy during calls.

risks.title: Higher bandwidth (~768 kbps/leg)
risks.mitigation: Fine for 1:1 voice; ~0.7 GB/hr two-way, within free-tier egress. If too heavy later, switch to native 16 kHz capture.

timeline.title: Removed decimation, switched to 48 kHz verbatim PCM
timeline.summary: Edited audio.js (capture48ToWire, playback rate), player-worklet.js (jitter buffer), main.js (batching + warning relaxation).

timeline.title: Syntax check + stale-ref grep
timeline.summary: All modules syntax-check; no stale decimation references remain.

decisions.title: Send 48 kHz PCM, no resampling
decisions.rationale: User chose this over native-16k or RNNoise-off. Eliminates the decimation artifacts while keeping RNNoise at its native rate; bandwidth ~768 kbps/leg is acceptable for 1:1.

validation.command: Grep confirms no stale decimate/_lp references (only an updated doc comment)
